verdict.rationale: Better Auth is an npm-installed TypeScript library that you instantiate inside your own app, and its docs say it 'requires a database to store user data' that you configure (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and more). Community users independently confirm 'all of your auth data in your own db', 'not tied to any db provider' and 'I own all the data'. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of self-managed deployment and data-residency topology, and a detailed list of supported database adapters beyond 'and more'.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can control where the auth system and its user data run — self-managed deployment, private instance, or my own database

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; export const auth = betterAuth({ //... });
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
It just works and I own all the data.
